sanskrit: jyeṣṭhaḥ putro dhṛtarāṣṭrasya mando; mūrkhaḥ śaṭhaḥ saṃjaya pāpaśīlaḥ praśāstā vai pṛthivī yena sarvā; suyodhanaṃ kuśalaṃ tāta pṛccheḥ
english: The eldest son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra is dull-witted, foolish, treacherous, and wicked in conduct, O Sañjaya — yet it is he by whom the whole earth is ruled. Ask after the welfare of Suyodhana, dear friend.

sanskrit: bhrātā kanīyān api tasya mandas; tathāśīlaḥ saṃjaya so 'pi śaśvat maheṣvāsaḥ śūratamaḥ kurūṇāṃ; duḥśāsanaṃ kuśalaṃ tāta pṛccheḥ
english: His younger brother is equally dull, of the same disposition, O Sañjaya — yet he is ever a great archer, the most valiant among the Kurus. Ask after the welfare of Duḥśāsana, dear friend.

sanskrit: vṛndārakaṃ kavim artheṣv amūḍhaṃ; mahāprajñaṃ sarvadharmopapannam na tasya yuddhaṃ rocate vai kadā cid; vaiśyāputraṃ kuśalaṃ tāta pṛccheḥ
english: Vrindara — the wise, never confused in matters of policy, of great intelligence, endowed with all virtues — he never approves of war at any time. Ask after the welfare of the son of the Vaiśya, dear friend.

sanskrit: nikartane devane yo 'dvitīyaś; channopadhaḥ sādhudevī matākṣaḥ yo durjayo devitavyena saṃkhye; sa citrasenaḥ kuśalaṃ tāta vācyaḥ
english: He who is unrivaled at dicing and gambling, of concealed stratagems, skilled at playing with dice, he who is unconquerable in the battle of dice — that Citrasena should be asked of his welfare, dear friend.

sanskrit: yasya kāmo vartate nityam eva; nānyaḥ śamād bhāratānām iti sma sa bāhlikānām ṛṣabho manasvī; purā yathā mābhivadet prasannaḥ
english: He whose constant desire has ever been that there be no other way for the Bharatas than peace — that bull of the Bāhlīkas, noble-minded, may he greet me with affection as he did before.

sanskrit: guṇair anekaiḥ pravaraiś ca yukto; vijñānavān naiva ca niṣṭhuro yaḥ snehād amarṣaṃ sahate sadaiva; sa somadattaḥ pūjanīyo mato me
english: Endowed with many excellent virtues, possessed of wisdom and never harsh, he who always bears anger out of affection — that Somadatta is worthy of reverence in my estimation.

sanskrit: arhattamaḥ kuruṣu saumadattiḥ; sa no bhrātā saṃjaya matsakhā ca maheṣvāso rathinām uttamo yaḥ; sahāmātyaḥ kuśalaṃ tasya pṛccheḥ
english: Somadatta's son is the most worthy among the Kurus — he is our brother, O Sañjaya, and also my friend, a great bowman, the foremost of chariot-warriors. Ask after his welfare together with his ministers.

sanskrit: ye caivānye kurumukhyā yuvānaḥ; putrāḥ pautrā bhrātaraś caiva ye naḥ yaṃ yam eṣāṃ yena yenābhigaccher; anāmayaṃ madvacanena vācyaḥ
english: And whatever other young foremost Kurus there are — sons, grandsons, and brothers of ours — whichever of them you approach in turn, each shall be greeted with my words asking of his health.

sanskrit: ye rājānaḥ pāṇḍavāyodhanāya; samānītā dhārtarāṣṭreṇa ke cit vasātayaḥ śālvakāḥ kekayāś ca; tathāmbaṣṭhā ye trigartāś ca mukhyāḥ
english: The kings who have been assembled by the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra for battle against the Pāṇḍavas — the Vasatas, the Salvakas, the Kekayas, the Ambaṣṭhas, and the foremost of the Trigartas —

sanskrit: prācyodīcyā dākṣiṇātyāś ca śūrās; tathā pratīcyāḥ pārvatīyāś ca sarve anṛśaṃsāḥ śīlavṛttopapannās; teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ kuśalaṃ tāta pṛccheḥ
english: — the heroes from the east and the north, from the south, and from the west and the mountains — all who are not cruel, who are endowed with good character and conduct — ask after the welfare of all of them, dear friend.

sanskrit: hastyārohā rathinaḥ sādinaś ca; padātayaś cāryasaṃghā mahāntaḥ ākhyāya māṃ kuśalinaṃ sma teṣām; anāmayaṃ paripṛccheḥ samagrān
english: The elephant-riders, the chariot-warriors, the cavalry, the infantry, and the great assemblies of noble men — having announced that I am well, inquire of the health of all of them in full.

sanskrit: tathā rājño hy arthayuktān amātyān; dauvārikān ye ca senāṃ nayanti āyavyayaṃ ye gaṇayanti yuktā; arthāṃś ca ye mahataś cintayanti
english: Likewise the ministers of the king who are skilled in statecraft, the door-keepers, those who lead the army, those who are diligently reckoning income and expenditure, and those who deliberate on great affairs —

sanskrit: gāndhārarājaḥ śakuniḥ pārvatīyo; nikartane yo 'dvitīyo 'kṣadevī mānaṃ kurvan dhārtarāṣṭrasya sūta; mithyābuddheḥ kuśalaṃ tāta pṛccheḥ
english: Śakuni, the king of the Gāndhāras, the mountain-dweller, who is unrivaled at gambling and cheating at dice, who feeds the pride of the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, that one of crooked intellect — ask of his welfare, dear friend.

sanskrit: yaḥ pāṇḍavān ekarathena vīraḥ; samutsahaty apradhṛṣyān vijetum yo muhyatāṃ mohayitādvitīyo; vaikartanaṃ kuśalaṃ tāta pṛccheḥ
english: He who, a hero, ventures with a single chariot to conquer the invincible Pāṇḍavas, who is unrivaled at confusing the bewildered — ask after the welfare of Vaikartana (Karṇa), dear friend.

sanskrit: sa eva bhaktaḥ sa guruḥ sa bhṛtyaḥ; sa vai pitā sa ca mātā suhṛc ca agādhabuddhir viduro dīrghadarśī; sa no mantrī kuśalaṃ tāta pṛccheḥ
english: He alone is the devoted one, he is the teacher, he is the servant, he is the father, he is the mother, and he is the friend — Vidura of unfathomable wisdom and far-sighted vision, our counselor. Ask of his welfare, dear friend.

sanskrit: vṛddhāḥ striyo yāś ca guṇopapannā; yā jñāyante saṃjaya mātaras tāḥ tābhiḥ sarvābhiḥ sahitābhiḥ sametya; strībhir vṛddhābhiḥ abhivādaṃ vadethāḥ
english: The aged women who are endowed with virtue, those known, O Sañjaya, as the mothers — meeting together with all of them, those aged women, pay them reverent salutation.

sanskrit: kaccit putrā jīvaputrāḥ susamyag; vartante vo vṛttim anṛśaṃsarūpām iti smoktvā saṃjaya brūhi paścād; ajātaśatruḥ kuśalī saputraḥ
english: "Do your sons, whose sons are living, rightly follow the conduct that is free from cruelty?" — having said this much, O Sañjaya, then say afterward: "Ajātaśatru is well, together with his sons."

sanskrit: yā no bhāryāḥ saṃjaya vettha tatra; tāsāṃ sarvāsāṃ kuśalaṃ tāta pṛccheḥ susaṃguptāḥ surabhayo 'navadyāḥ; kaccid gṛhān āvasathāpramattāḥ
english: The wives of ours that you know to be there, O Sañjaya — ask after the welfare of all of them, dear friend. Are they well-guarded, fragrant, blameless, and do they dwell in the household without negligence?

sanskrit: kaccid vṛttiṃ śvaśureṣu bhadrāḥ; kalyāṇīṃ vartadhvam anṛśaṃsarūpām yathā ca vaḥ syuḥ patayo 'nukūlās; tathā vṛttim ātmanaḥ sthāpayadhvam
english: "Do you, O auspicious ones, follow a good and benevolent conduct toward your fathers-in-law? And just as you would have your husbands favorable to you, so establish your own conduct accordingly."

sanskrit: yā naḥ snuṣāḥ saṃjaya vettha tatra; prāptāḥ kulebhyaś ca guṇopapannāḥ prajāvatyo brūhi sametya tāś ca; yudhiṣṭhiro vo 'bhyavadat prasannaḥ
english: The daughters-in-law of ours that you know to be there, O Sañjaya — who have come from good families and are endowed with virtue, who have children — meeting them also, say to them: "Yudhiṣṭhira greeted you with affection."

sanskrit: kanyāḥ svajethāḥ sadaneṣu saṃjaya; anāmayaṃ madvacanena pṛṣṭvā kalyāṇā vaḥ santu patayo 'nukūlā; yūyaṃ patīnāṃ bhavatānukūlāḥ
english: The maidens you should embrace in their dwellings, O Sañjaya, having inquired of their health with my words: "May you have auspicious and favorable husbands; may you be favorable to your husbands."

sanskrit: alaṃkṛtā vastravatyaḥ sugandhā; abībhatsāḥ sukhitā bhogavatyaḥ laghu yāsāṃ darśanaṃ vāk ca laghvī; veśastriyaḥ kuśalaṃ tāta pṛccheḥ
english: The courtesans — adorned with ornaments, clothed, fragrant, not repulsive, happy, and enjoying pleasures — whose appearance is charming and whose speech is graceful, ask of their welfare, dear friend.

sanskrit: dāsīputrā ye ca dāsāḥ kurūṇāṃ; tadāśrayā bahavaḥ kubjakhañjāḥ ākhyāya māṃ kuśalinaṃ sma tebhyo; anāmayaṃ paripṛccher jaghanyam
english: The sons of maidservants, and the servants of the Kurus, and the many hunchbacks and lame persons who depend on them — having announced that I am well, inquire last of their health.

sanskrit: kaccid vṛttir vartate vai purāṇī; kaccid bhogān dhārtarāṣṭro dadāti aṅgahīnān kṛpaṇān vāmanāṃś ca; ānṛśaṃsyād dhṛtarāṣṭro bibharti
english: Does the ancient custom still hold? Does the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra give them their enjoyments? The cripples, the destitute, and the dwarfs — does Dhṛtarāṣṭra maintain them out of compassion?

sanskrit: andhāś ca sarve sthavirās tathaiva; hastājīvā bahavo ye 'tra santi ākhyāya māṃ kuśalinaṃ sma teṣām; anāmayaṃ paripṛccher jaghanyam
english: All the blind and the aged, and the many who earn their living by the work of their hands who are there — having announced that I am well, inquire last of their health.

sanskrit: mā bhaiṣṭa duḥkhena kujīvitena; nūnaṃ kṛtaṃ paralokeṣu pāpam nigṛhya śatrūn suhṛdo 'nugṛhya; vāsobhir annena ca vo bhariṣye
english: "Do not be afraid of misery and a wretched life — surely sins were committed in former worlds. Having subdued enemies and blessed my friends, I will provide you with clothing and food."

sanskrit: santy eva me brāhmaṇebhyaḥ kṛtāni; bhāvīny atho no bata vartayanti paśyāmy ahaṃ yuktarūpāṃs tathaiva; tām eva siddhiṃ śrāvayethā nṛpaṃ tam
english: There are indeed those acts of mine done for the Brāhmaṇas that are yet to bear fruit — yet alas, they do not sustain us. I see those also as being in a fitting form. Report that very outcome to that king.

sanskrit: ye cānāthā durbalāḥ sarvakālam; ātmany eva prayatante 'tha mūḍhāḥ tāṃś cāpi tvaṃ kṛpaṇān sarvathaiva; asmadvākyāt kuśalaṃ tāta pṛccheḥ
english: Those who are helpless and feeble at all times, who strive only for themselves and are confused — those wretched ones as well, in every way, ask after their welfare with my words, dear friend.

sanskrit: ye cāpy anye saṃśritā dhārtarāṣṭrān; nānādigbhyo 'bhyāgatāḥ sūtaputra dṛṣṭvā tāṃś caivārhataś cāpi sarvān; saṃpṛcchethāḥ kuśalaṃ cāvyayaṃ ca
english: And whatever others have taken refuge with the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who have come from various directions, O son of a charioteer — having seen all of them and those worthy of honor, inquire of their welfare and their undiminished prosperity.

sanskrit: evaṃ sarvānāgatābhyāgatāṃś ca; rājño dūtān sarvadigbhyo 'bhyupetān pṛṣṭvā sarvān kuśalaṃ tāṃś ca sūta; paścād ahaṃ kuśalī teṣu vācyaḥ
english: Having thus inquired of all those who have not arrived and those who have arrived, and the envoys of kings who have come from all directions — having asked them all of their welfare, O charioteer's son, afterward I shall be announced as well among them.

sanskrit: na hīdṛśāḥ santy apare pṛthivyāṃ; ye yodhakā dhārtarāṣṭreṇa labdhāḥ dharmas tu nityo mama dharma eva; mahābalaḥ śatrunibarhaṇāya
english: There are no others like them on the earth — the warriors that have been obtained by the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra. But righteousness is eternal; my righteousness alone is a great force for the destruction of enemies.

sanskrit: idaṃ punar vacanaṃ dhārtarāṣṭraṃ; suyodhanaṃ saṃjaya śrāvayethāḥ yas te śarīre hṛdayaṃ dunoti; kāmaḥ kurūn asapatno 'nuśiṣyām
english: This further message, O Sañjaya, you should convey to Suyodhana, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra: "The desire that torments your heart in your body — I shall instruct the Kurus without a rival."

sanskrit: na vidyate yuktir etasya kā cin; naivaṃvidhāḥ syāma yathā priyaṃ te dadasva vā śakrapuraṃ mamaiva; yudhyasva vā bhāratamukhya vīra
english: There is no expedient in this matter. We would not be such as to please you. Either give me Indra's city as my own, or fight — O foremost of the Bharatas, O hero.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca uta santam asantaṃ ca bālaṃ vṛddhaṃ ca saṃjaya utābalaṃ balīyāṃsaṃ dhātā prakurute vaśe
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The Creator brings under his sway, O Sañjaya, both the virtuous and the wicked, both the young and the old, both the weak and the strong.

sanskrit: uta bālāya pāṇḍityaṃ paṇḍitāyota bālatām dadāti sarvam īśānaḥ purastāc chukram uccaran
english: The Lord of all, the seminal source from the beginning, grants wisdom to a child and childishness to a wise man.

sanskrit: alaṃ vijñāpanāya syād ācakṣīthā yathātatham atho mantraṃ mantrayitvā anyonyenātihṛṣṭavat
english: Enough of informing — you should report things as they truly are. And then, having deliberated on the counsel among ourselves, we were exceedingly glad of one another.

sanskrit: gāvalgaṇe kurūn gatvā dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ mahābalam abhivādyopasaṃgṛhya tataḥ pṛccher anāmayam
english: O son of Gavalgaṇa, going to the Kurus, approach the mighty Dhṛtarāṣṭra with reverence and, having clasped his feet, then inquire of his health.

sanskrit: brūyāś cainaṃ tvam āsīnaṃ kurubhiḥ parivāritam tavaiva rājan vīryeṇa sukhaṃ jīvanti pāṇḍavāḥ
english: And you should say to him as he sits surrounded by the Kurus: "By your own prowess, O king, the Pāṇḍavas live happily."

sanskrit: tava prasādād bālās te prāptā rājyam ariṃdama rājye tān sthāpayitvāgre nopekṣīr vinaśiṣyataḥ
english: "By your grace, those children attained the kingdom, O subduer of foes. Having established them in the kingdom before, do not now disregard them as they are about to perish."

sanskrit: sarvam apy etad ekasya nālaṃ saṃjaya kasya cit tāta saṃhatya jīvāmo mā dviṣadbhyo vaśaṃ gamaḥ
english: All of this together is not enough for any single one, O Sañjaya. Let us live united, dear one — let us not fall into the power of our enemies.

sanskrit: tathā bhīṣmaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ bhāratānāṃ pitāmaham śirasābhivadethās tvaṃ mama nāma prakīrtayan
english: Likewise pay reverent salutation with your head to Bhīṣma, the son of Shantanu, the grandsire of the Bharatas, while announcing my name.

sanskrit: abhivādya ca vaktavyas tato 'smākaṃ pitāmahaḥ bhavatā śaṃtanor vaṃśo nimagnaḥ punar uddhṛtaḥ
english: Having paid reverence, then say to our grandsire: "By you the lineage of Shantanu, which had sunk down, has been raised up again."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ kuru tathā tāta svamatena pitāmaha yathā jīvanti te pautrāḥ prītimantaḥ parasparam
english: "So do accordingly, dear grandfather, by your own judgment, that your grandsons may live with affection for one another."

sanskrit: tathaiva viduraṃ brūyāḥ kurūṇāṃ mantradhāriṇam ayuddhaṃ saumya bhāṣasva hitakāmo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Likewise speak to Vidura, the keeper of counsel among the Kurus: "Speak for non-war, O gentle one — Yudhiṣṭhira, desiring your welfare, asks this."

sanskrit: atho suyodhanaṃ brūyā rājaputram amarṣaṇam madhye kurūṇām āsīnam anunīya punaḥ punaḥ
english: And then speak to Suyodhana, the intolerant prince, as he sits in the midst of the Kurus, persuading him again and again.

sanskrit: apaśyan mām upekṣantaṃ kṛṣṇām ekāṃ sabhāgatām tadduḥkham atitikṣāma mā vadhīṣma kurūn iti
english: "Not seeing me and disregarding Kṛṣṇa alone as she was dragged to the assembly — we endured that grief. Let us not slay the Kurus, so we said."

sanskrit: evaṃ pūrvāparān kleśān atitikṣanta pāṇḍavāḥ yathā balīyasaḥ santas tat sarvaṃ kuravo viduḥ
english: Thus the Pāṇḍavas endured the earlier and later sufferings — even though they were the stronger — and all of this the Kurus know well.

sanskrit: yan naḥ prāvrājayaḥ saumya ajinaiḥ prativāsitān tadduḥkham atitikṣāma mā vadhīṣma kurūn iti
english: "That you sent us into exile, O gentle one, clad in the skins of deer — we endured that grief. Let us not slay the Kurus, so we said."

sanskrit: yat tat sabhāyām ākramya kṛṣṇāṃ keśeṣv adharṣayat duḥśāsanas te 'numate tac cāsmābhir upekṣitam
english: "That which Duḥśāsana, with your sanction, did — seizing Kṛṣṇa in the assembly and dragging her by the hair — that too was overlooked by us."

sanskrit: yathocitaṃ svakaṃ bhāgaṃ labhemahi paraṃtapa nivartaya paradravye buddhiṃ gṛddhāṃ nararṣabha
english: "Let us obtain our rightful and proper share, O scorcher of foes. Turn away the greedy mind fixed on another's wealth, O bull among men."

sanskrit: śāntir evaṃ bhaved rājan prītiś caiva parasparam rājyaikadeśam api naḥ prayaccha śamam icchatām
english: "Thus there would be peace, O king, and mutual affection as well. Even a part of the kingdom give to us who desire peace."

sanskrit: kuśasthalaṃ vṛkasthalam āsandī vāraṇāvatam avasānaṃ bhaved atra kiṃ cid eva tu pañcamam
english: "Kushasthala, Vrikasthala, Asandi, Vāraṇāvata — and some fifth place as the settlement — let it be so here."

sanskrit: bhrātṝṇāṃ dehi pañcānāṃ grāmān pañca suyodhana śāntir no 'stu mahāprājña jñātibhiḥ saha saṃjaya
english: "Give five villages to the five brothers, O Suyodhana. Let there be peace for us, O greatly wise one, together with our kinsmen, O Sañjaya."

sanskrit: bhrātā bhrātaram anvetu pitā putreṇa yujyatām smayamānāḥ samāyāntu pāñcālāḥ kurubhiḥ saha
english: "Let brother seek out brother, let the father be united with his son. Let the Pāñcālas come smiling together with the Kurus."

sanskrit: akṣatān kurupāñcālān paśyema iti kāmaye sarve sumanasas tāta śāmyāma bharatarṣabha
english: "I desire that we may see the Kurus and Pāñcālas unharmed. Let all of us, dear one, be of good cheer and be at peace, O bull of the Bharatas."

sanskrit: alam eva śamāyāsmi tathā yuddhāya saṃjaya dharmārthayor alaṃ cāhaṃ mṛdave dāruṇāya ca
english: I am indeed ready for peace and equally for war, O Sañjaya. I am also ready for righteousness and for gain, for mildness and for severity.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca anujñātaḥ pāṇḍavena prayayau saṃjayas tadā śāsanaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya sarvaṃ kṛtvā mahātmanaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Permitted by the Pāṇḍava, Sañjaya departed, having carried out all the commands of the great-souled Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: saṃprāpya hāstinapuraṃ śīghraṃ ca praviveśa ha antaḥpuram upasthāya dvāḥsthaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Having reached Hāstinapura, he entered quickly, and approaching the inner palace, he spoke these words to the doorkeeper:

sanskrit: ācakṣva māṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrāya dvāḥstha; upāgataṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ sakāśāt jāgarti ced abhivades tvaṃ hi kṣattaḥ; praviśeyaṃ vidito bhūmipasya
english: "Announce me to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O doorkeeper — I have arrived from the presence of the Pāṇḍavas. If he is awake, you should inform Kṣattṛ (Vidura), and I may enter when I am known to the king of the earth."

sanskrit: dvāḥstha uvāca saṃjayo 'yaṃ bhūmipate namas te; didṛkṣayā dvāram upāgatas te prāpto dūtaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ sakāśāt; praśādhi rājan kim ayaṃ karotu
english: The doorkeeper said: O lord of the earth, homage to you — this Sañjaya, the envoy arrived from the presence of the Pāṇḍavas, has come to your door desiring to see you. Command, O king, what he should do.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca ācakṣva māṃ sukhinaṃ kālyam asmai; praveśyatāṃ svāgataṃ saṃjayāya na cāham etasya bhavāmy akālyaḥ; sa me kasmād dvāri tiṣṭheta kṣattaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Announce to him that I am well and that this is an auspicious hour. Let Sañjaya be welcomed and admitted. I am not unwilling for him at this time — why should he stand at my door, O Kṣattṛ?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ praviśyānumate nṛpasya; mahad veśma prājñaśūrāryaguptam siṃhāsanasthaṃ pārthivam āsasāda; vaicitravīryaṃ prāñjaliḥ sūtaputraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, entering with the king's permission, the son of a charioteer reached the great palace guarded by the wise, the brave, and the noble, and approached the son of Vicitravīrya seated on his lion-throne, with joined palms.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca saṃjayo 'haṃ bhūmipate namas te; prāpto 'smi gatvā naradeva pāṇḍavān abhivādya tvāṃ pāṇḍuputro manasvī; yudhiṣṭhiraḥ kuśalaṃ cānvapṛcchat
english: Sañjaya said: I am Sañjaya, O lord of the earth — homage to you. I have come, O king of men, having gone to the Pāṇḍavas. The noble-minded son of Pāṇḍu, Yudhiṣṭhira, has also inquired of your welfare.

sanskrit: sa te putrān pṛcchati prīyamāṇaḥ; kaccit putraiḥ prīyase naptṛbhiś ca tathā suhṛdbhiḥ sacivaiś ca rājan; ye cāpi tvām upajīvanti taiś ca
english: He asks of your sons with affection: "Are you pleased with your sons and your grandsons, and with your friends and ministers, O king, and with those also who depend on you for their livelihood?"

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca abhyetya tvāṃ tāta vadāmi saṃjaya; ajātaśatruṃ ca sukhena pārtham kaccit sa rājā kuśalī saputraḥ; sahāmātyaḥ sānujaḥ kauravāṇām
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Coming to you, dear Sañjaya, I say — is that king, Ajātaśatru, the son of Pāṇḍu, well, together with his sons, his ministers, and his younger brothers, among the Kauravas?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca sahāmātyaḥ kuśalī pāṇḍuputro; bhūyaś cāto yac ca te 'gre mano 'bhūt nirṇiktadharmārthakaro manasvī; bahuśruto dṛṣṭimāñ śīlavāṃś ca
english: Sañjaya said: The son of Pāṇḍu is well together with his ministers. And furthermore, what you previously had in your mind — he who carries out righteousness and gain with purity, who is noble-minded, well-versed in scripture, of far-sighted wisdom, and possessed of good character —

sanskrit: paraṃ dharmāt pāṇḍavasyānṛśaṃsyaṃ; dharmaḥ paro vittacayān mato 'sya sukhapriye dharmahīne na pārtho; 'nurudhyate bhārata tasya viddhi
english: — the highest virtue of the Pāṇḍava is his freedom from cruelty; righteousness is rated by him higher than the accumulation of wealth. The son of Pṛthā does not accommodate what is dear and pleasant when it is devoid of righteousness — know this of him, O Bharata.

sanskrit: paraprayuktaḥ puruṣo viceṣṭate; sūtraprotā dārumayīva yoṣā imaṃ dṛṣṭvā niyamaṃ pāṇḍavasya; manye paraṃ karma daivaṃ manuṣyāt
english: A man acts when impelled by another, like a wooden puppet threaded on a string. Seeing this restraint of the Pāṇḍava, I consider fate to be superior to human action.

sanskrit: imaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā tava karmadoṣaṃ; pādodarkaṃ ghoram avarṇarūpam yāvan naraḥ kāmayate 'tikālyaṃ; tāvan naro 'yaṃ labhate praśaṃsām
english: And seeing this fault in your conduct — which will have terrible consequences in the end, of an ignoble nature — as long as a man desires exceeding good fortune, so long does this man win praise.

sanskrit: ajātaśatrus tu vihāya pāpaṃ; jīrṇāṃ tvacaṃ sarpa ivāsamarthām virocate 'hāryavṛttena dhīro; yudhiṣṭhiras tvayi pāpaṃ visṛjya
english: But Ajātaśatru, the steadfast Yudhiṣṭhira, having cast off sin like a serpent shedding its worn-out skin, shines with conduct that cannot be taken away, having left the sin with you.

sanskrit: aṅgātmanaḥ karma nibodha rājan; dharmārthayuktād āryavṛttād apetam upakrośaṃ ceha gato 'si rājan; noheś ca pāpaṃ prasajed amutra
english: Understand the action of your own limbs, O king — that which is devoid of righteousness, gain, and noble conduct. You have incurred reproach here, O king; do not let sin also cling to you in the next world.

sanskrit: sa tvam arthaṃ saṃśayitaṃ vinā tair; āśaṃsase putravaśānugo 'dya adharmaśabdaś ca mahān pṛthivyāṃ; nedaṃ karma tvatsamaṃ bhāratāgrya
english: You, subjugated by your sons, now hope for doubtful gain without them. And a great cry of unrighteousness spreads through the earth — this conduct is not worthy of you, O foremost of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: hīnaprajño dauṣkuleyo nṛśaṃso; dīrghavairī kṣatravidyāsv adhīraḥ evaṃdharmā nāpadaḥ saṃtitīrṣed; dhīnavīryo yaś ca bhaved aśiṣṭaḥ
english: One of inferior understanding, of low birth, cruel, nursing long enmity, unsteady in the knowledge of the warrior's art — a man of such qualities cannot cross over misfortune, and he who is of feeble valor becomes ungoverned.

sanskrit: kule jāto dharmavān yo yaśasvī; bahuśrutaḥ sukhajīvī yatātmā dharmārthayor grathitayor bibharti; nānyatra diṣṭasya vaśād upaiti
english: He who is born of good family, righteous, illustrious, well-versed in scripture, living happily, self-controlled — he bears the intertwined weight of righteousness and gain; he does not stray beyond the sway of destiny.

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi mantrāgryadharo manīṣī; dharmārthayor āpadi saṃpraṇetā evaṃyuktaḥ sarvamantrair ahīno; anānṛśaṃsyaṃ karma kuryād amūḍhaḥ
english: How indeed could an intelligent man, holding the chief counsel, a guide for righteousness and gain in times of crisis, thus endowed and not lacking in any counsel, the unconfused one, perform an act of cruelty?

sanskrit: tavāpīme mantravidaḥ sametya; samāsate karmasu nityayuktāḥ teṣām ayaṃ balavān niścayaś ca; kurukṣayārthe nirayo vyapādi
english: Your own counselors, versed in counsel, assembling together, remain ever engaged in affairs. And this is the strong resolve of theirs — the destruction of the Kurus has been directed toward ruin.

sanskrit: akālikaṃ kuravo nābhaviṣyan; pāpena cet pāpam ajātaśatruḥ icchej jātu tvayi pāpaṃ visṛjya; nindā ceyaṃ tava loke 'bhaviṣyat
english: The Kurus would not have met an untimely end, if Ajātaśatru were ever to wish evil for evil — if he desired to visit sin upon you. And this blame of yours would have spread through the world.

sanskrit: kim anyatra viṣayād īśvarāṇāṃ; yatra pārthaḥ paralokaṃ dadarśa atyakrāmat sa tathā saṃmataḥ syān; na saṃśayo nāsti manuṣyakāraḥ
english: What domain is there other than that of the lords of the earth, where the son of Pṛthā could behold and transcend even the next world? He would be regarded in that way without doubt — there is no human agency involved.

sanskrit: etān guṇān karmakṛtān avekṣya; bhāvābhāvau vartamānāv anityau balir hi rājā pāram avindamāno; nānyat kālāt kāraṇaṃ tatra mene
english: Observing these virtues accomplished by deeds, existence and non-existence both present and impermanent — King Bali, not finding his way to the other shore, deemed there to be no cause in that other than Time.

sanskrit: cakṣuḥ śrotre nāsikā tvak ca jihvā; jñānasyaitāny āyatanāni jantoḥ tāni prītāny eva tṛṣṇākṣayānte; tāny avyatho duḥkhahīnaḥ praṇudyāt
english: The eye, the ear, the nose, the skin, and the tongue — these are the seats of knowledge for a living being. At the end of the extinction of craving, they rest in contentment; the one without pain and free from suffering should push them away.
